newsitem.title: UK: Yeltsin gives Russia debt price a helping hand.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin gives Russia debt price a helping hand.

text.p: Russian debt firmed on Thursday after President Boris Yeltsin's address to parliament.
But traders said Russian and other emerging country debt prices for the moment remain very much in the shadow of U.S. financial markets and the individual country news is having only limited impact.

"It was a relief that Yeltsin looked reasonably healthy. He sounded fairly positive. But his speech is less significant at the moment than the overall situation (in emerging markets)," one Russian debt trader said.
In early trading, dollar Vneshekonombank paper -- old Soviet debt which is close to being restructured into loans -- rose 3/8 of a point to 80-3/8 cents in the dollar.

Though above recent lows, it is well below the more than 87 cent high touched last week before emerging markets plunged on remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan which were taken as suggesting an early rise in interest rates.

Russian MinFins, however, showed a bigger rise but the spreads on Russia's Eurobond barely moved after having fallen over the past week to around 340 basis points, the level at which the bond was issued in November. -- Jonathan Thatcher, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7770
